description:
No spec subject — bookkeeping epic.

Impromptu epic created 2026-07-27 to land 21 independently-surfaced follow-up tickets on a SINGLE PR as release 0.11.0. Children were each carved by an earlier ticket cold verification, critical review, or the 0.9.6 / 0.10.0 fast-follow sweeps, and had no owning epic.

## BASE AND RELEASE

REBASED 2026-07-27. This epic originally branched from feat/specled_-td7-self-identifying-descriptors to keep specled_-td7 and specled_-n5s on the same PR. That branch has since MERGED to main as 02258a0b (PR #30, release 0.10.0), so td7 and n5s are shipped and are NO LONGER part of this epic. Main then advanced again with 2023373d (PR #31, worktree workflow host-elixir 0.22.0 -> 0.23.0).

This epic now branches from main at 2023373d and targets release 0.11.0. VERSION in tree is 0.10.0 (the shipped value); the release step bumps it to 0.11.0 and opens a NEW CHANGELOG section. There is no pre-opened section to extend.

## ADMISSION VERIFICATION (2026-07-27)

All 22 candidate tickets were cold-verified by one fresh-context agent each before this epic was formed. Result: zero already_done, zero obsolete. One premise_wrong (specled_-4pl) and three partially_done (specled_-26g, specled_-npo, specled_-4f7) had their mandates narrowed or rewritten during admission — see the per-ticket ADMISSION comments, which SUPERSEDE those four descriptions. specled_-4a6 was verified still_applicable but CUT from this epic by user decision; see its comment.

Verification ran against tree e81f9f98, which is content-identical to what merged as 02258a0b. Ticket line-number citations therefore still resolve on this base. The one thing that changed underfoot is the worktree tooling (make/worktree.mk is new) — see the orientation comment.

## SEQUENCING RATIONALE

Waves are derived from a file-collision map, not from caution. Every serialization names the file the two tickets share; tickets with disjoint file sets run concurrently.

Wave 1 (12, fully parallel): wby, ako, yds, vbo, pii, ehv, dn4.12, npo, zek, z5t, chb, 4pl
Wave 2 (7, each behind exactly one Wave-1 ticket): 26g<-ehv, asb<-ehv, zd8<-dn4.12, b23<-dn4.12, ozm<-4pl+ehv, 14t<-zek, 4f7<-pii
Wave 3 (2): xkn.1<-26g+npo, xkn.2<-z5t+ozm

Orchestrated by /orchestrate-epic.

Five children (ako, ozm, yds, zek, asb) mandate proving a new assertion RED under a named mutation. "Tests pass" is not evidence for these. Require the mutation and its revert in the commit message; bounce otherwise.

tagged_tests verification legs are load-flaky under concurrency. Never run bare `mix spec.check` while implementation agents are running - agents use `--no-run-commands`; exactly one serial bare run in Wave 4. Re-run a single red leg serially before treating it as real.

LESSONS
- [stale-spec] A decision record must describe the remedy the commit actually shipped; never transcribe a mandate's wording when the diff implements something different (from specled_-ehv)
- [stale-spec] Before writing a prescription into an ADR, check it is SATISFIABLE by the code it governs — a rule that can only be followed vacuously is worse than the sentence it replaced (from specled_-ehv)

LESSONS (append)
- [other] A grader must post its verdict to the ticket it actually graded — check the ticket id in the `bw comment` argument before posting. A mis-pasted marker corrupts the orchestrator's phase reconstruction on resume (from specled_-dn4.12)
- [untested-clause] When a ticket's defining invariant is a branch flag, the test must pick an input where the two branches DISAGREE. An input where both branches agree by construction cannot go red and does not pin the split (from specled_-dn4.12)

LESSONS (append)
- [other] `mix format --check-formatted` is a declared merge gate in CLAUDE.md and must be run before completion on EVERY ticket, even when the ticket's Verification section omits it. Hand-wrapping a call the formatter would collapse is the usual way it fails (from specled_-ehv)

ORCHESTRATOR CORRECTION: the SCOPE CONTRACT comments posted for the wave-1 tickets
ehv, 4pl, dn4.12, npo, z5t and pii omitted `mix format --check-formatted` from their
Verification sections. That was an orchestrator omission, not an implementer miss.
The delegated-implementer prompt template has been amended so every subsequent spawn
carries the requirement unconditionally; the six affected tickets get it via this
lessons block and, where already bounced, via their bounce comment.

LESSONS (append) — ROOT CAUSE of the two mis-posted verdicts

Both stray comments (on specled_-dn4.12 at 10:27:33Z and on specled_-z5t) have the
same cause, now identified by the z5t verifier:

The session scratchpad is SHARED across every agent. Graders were writing their comment
bodies to generic filenames there (`verify.txt`, `ehv_comment.txt`, ...). zsh runs with
`noclobber`, so a `>` redirect onto an existing path FAILS SILENTLY from the agent's
point of view; the fallback `cat` then reads whatever a different agent left at that
path, and the agent posts another ticket's verdict under its own marker.

- [other] A grader must write its comment body to a UNIQUELY NAMED file — include the ticket id, e.g. `<scratchpad>/<ticket-id>.verify.txt` — and must use `>|` (or `rm -f` first) because zsh `noclobber` makes a plain `>` onto an existing file fail. Then re-read the file and confirm it names the ticket you graded BEFORE running `bw comment` (from specled_-dn4.12, specled_-z5t)

Orchestrator action: this instruction is now carried in every grader prompt. Both stray
comments are marked VOID on their tickets and were retracted by their posting agents;
neither changed a routing decision.

ORCHESTRATOR RULING — how the Selective Audit Gate's requirement-coverage clause is
being applied in this epic. Recorded so every routing decision here is auditable.

The clause reads: "Every `must` has both `covered by <test>` and a concrete
`Would fail if <failure>` line; none is `NOT COVERED`."

Subjects in this repo carry many `must` requirements (specled.mix_tasks has 27,
specled.package 6, specled.coverage_capture 41) while a typical ticket here touches
one. Verifiers have handled that two different ways, and the two are NOT equivalent:

MEETS THE CLAUSE — the verifier accounts for EVERY `must` individually: either a
`covered by` + `Would fail if` + `Seams:` line, or the requirement is NAMED and given
a checkable justification for being unreachable by this diff. Nothing is left silent.
  - specled_-wby: all 27 enumerated (9 in radius with coverage, 18 named individually
    with the justification that the diff touches no file they realize and the two
    shared surfaces are byte-unchanged). AUTO-APPROVED.
  - specled_-z5t: all 6 enumerated with per-requirement blast-radius reasoning.
    AUTO-APPROVED.
  - specled_-pii: no `Advances:` subject, so the clause is vacuous rather than
    skipped, and the verifier said so instead of fabricating entries. AUTO-APPROVED.

DOES NOT MEET IT — the verifier covers the touched requirement and disposes of the
rest as a group ("the remaining musts are not reachable", "not in this diff's blast
radius") without naming them. The claim may well be true, but it is unchecked, and an
unchecked group claim is exactly what silent omission looks like. These go to audit.
  - specled_-4pl and specled_-npo: routed to audit on this basis. Both audits then
    APPROVED after enumerating the requirements themselves and confirming the scoping
    held. Cost: one extra grader each. Correct call — the audit is what turned an
    assertion into a checked fact.

Rationale: the clause exists to stop a `must` being left unproven. Individual
enumeration satisfies that intent whether the disposition is "covered" or "cannot be
reached, here is why". A group dismissal does not, because nobody has looked.
This ruling is applied uniformly for the rest of the epic.

MERGE GATE — after specled_-pii close (epic head b06603fd). mix compile --warnings-as-errors: green. mix test: 3 properties, 1272 tests, 0 failures. mix format --check-formatted: green. mix deps.unlock --check-unused: green. mix spec.check --no-run-commands: see next line. Bare spec.check deferred to the single serial end-of-epic run per this epic's FLAKE POLICY. Closed so far: specled_-npo, specled_-pii.

LESSONS (append)
- [stale-spec] When a mandate hands you replacement prose, check it against the test before adopting it. specled_-zek's admission mandate said to "drop the positional word" but its supplied replacement text reintroduced a positional claim ("in the resume-timeout suffix") that no assertion proves. Applying supplied text faithfully is not a defence if the text is wrong (from specled_-zek)
- [stale-spec] A requirement and the scenario that covers it are one contract. Reword one and you must reword the other, or the subject states the contract two different ways and the over-claim you set out to remove is still in the file (from specled_-zek)

LESSONS (append)
- [untested-clause] A guard that enumerates FORBIDDEN spellings is only as good as the enumeration. specled_-vbo caught `github.event.pull_request.head.sha` but not `${{ github.head_ref }}`, `$GITHUB_HEAD_REF`, or `gh pr checkout` — documented aliases for the same value. When a requirement forbids an ACT, prefer deny-by-default over a denylist: allowlist the permitted shapes and reject the rest (from specled_-vbo)
- [other] Mutation testing must be ADVERSARIAL, not confirmatory. specled_-vbo's first verifier mutated four clauses, saw RED, and passed the ticket — while two evasions were live. Its second verifier ran 21 mutants plus an unmutated control (so the harness could be shown not trivially red) and found four more. Design mutants to BEAT the guard, not to confirm it (from specled_-vbo)
